nodes.label: OSC Internal Knowledge Assistant
nodes.rationale: A provider-agnostic RAG question-answering service over OSC's internal documents. Retrieves passages, generates a grounded answer, attaches citations, and abstains rather than guessing when the corpus does not support an answer. Status: Phase 2, verified end to end on a local stack, not production-ready.

nodes.label: Vendor Agnosticism (the distinguishing constraint)
nodes.rationale: Chat model, embedding model, reranker, vector store and chunker are each selected by configuration and swappable independently, because the team expects to swap LLMs/embedders/rerankers frequently and that must be cheap. Enforced by one rule: business logic imports `protocols` and `types` only and never imports a provider module — checkable with a grep. 13 chat providers, 11 embedding providers, 3 rerankers, 3 vector stores, 2 chunkers registered; adding another is a new file plus one import line.

nodes.label: The Five Protocol Seams
nodes.rationale: Structural typing (Protocol), not base classes: a provider is compatible by virtue of its shape. No inheritance, nothing to register beyond the factory, and a test double becomes indistinguishable from a real provider — which is what makes the API tests meaningful. Total surface is about 120 lines, which is also the evidence used to reject LangChain/LlamaIndex.

nodes.label: ChatModel Protocol
nodes.rationale: complete() / stream(); declares supports_citations so the citation capability flag lives in the adapter and no business logic branches on provider identity.

nodes.label: EmbeddingModel Protocol
nodes.rationale: embed_documents() / embed_query(); declares dimensions. The declared width is injected into the vector store by the container because the store cannot know it itself.

nodes.label: VectorStore Protocol
nodes.rationale: replace_document(), delete_document(), three search methods, hash listing. This protocol is explicitly named as the swap point where a dedicated vector database would be introduced if vector search p95 degrades or the corpus exceeds a few million chunks.

nodes.label: Reranker Protocol
nodes.rationale: rerank(query, candidates, top_k). Defaults to noop because there is no golden set to demonstrate the cross-encoder improves anything.

nodes.label: Chunker Protocol
nodes.rationale: split(document) -> list[Chunk].

nodes.label: Shared Domain Vocabulary (types.py)
nodes.rationale: Document, Chunk, EmbeddedChunk, ScoredChunk, ChatRequest, Citation, Answer — all frozen dataclasses, the only vocabulary shared across modules. Deliberately the largest shared surface so that business logic needs nothing else besides protocols. RetrievalResult is flagged as the only unfrozen dataclass, a known inconsistency.

nodes.label: Registry and Composition Root
nodes.rationale: Five Registry instances map a provider name to a factory; a provider module registers itself on import and container.py imports the providers package once, so nothing in the call path imports every possible implementation. Container builds components lazily via cached_property, so `osc-assistant ingest` never constructs a chat model and therefore never needs an LLM credential.

nodes.label: ComponentConfig as Architectural Hub
nodes.rationale: Betweenness centrality in the generated knowledge graph identifies ComponentConfig (bridging 15 communities) and Document (bridging 15) as the true architectural hubs — configuration and the corpus record are what the whole system routes through, which matches the intended design.

nodes.label: StubEmbeddingModel Is the Most Connected Node
nodes.rationale: A test double has 57 edges, more than VectorStore, Document or any real provider. The graph is reporting that the test suite, not production wiring, is what actually exercises every seam — expected when all providers are optional extras, but it means the seams are proven against stubs far more than against real providers.

nodes.label: Hybrid Retrieval by Default
nodes.rationale: Internal corpora are dense with acronyms, product codenames and error strings that semantic search handles badly, and paraphrase that keyword search handles badly. Postgres provides both indexes, so the marginal cost is one query and a fusion step. Explicitly framed as avoiding a known failure mode, not premature optimisation.

nodes.label: Reciprocal Rank Fusion (dual implementation)
nodes.rationale: The same RRF formula is implemented twice — in fusion.py for the memory store and in SQL inside the pgvector store — deliberately, so both stores rank identically and swapping the vector store cannot change result ordering.

nodes.label: Abstention Is Architectural, Not a Prompt
nodes.rationale: No retrieval hits means the model is never called, because generating from nothing is guessing. No citations means the answer is treated as ungrounded. In streaming mode the final `complete` event is authoritative and the client discards what it already rendered — a policy that only held when not streaming would be worse than none.

nodes.label: Grounded Generation with Citations
nodes.rationale: The answerer builds a ChatRequest with a frozen system prompt and the retrieved chunks as sources; both citation paths converge on one Citation shape so nothing downstream branches on provider.

nodes.label: Native Citations Where Available, Markers Elsewhere
nodes.rationale: Anthropic passes sources as structured documents and returns per-span citations verified against the source text; every other provider renders sources into the prompt and parses [n] markers back out. Both produce the same Citation object, so nothing downstream — including the UI — can tell the difference. A deliberate trade-off for vendor agnosticism: the first verifies a citation, the second only asserts one. The gap is supposed to be quantified by the evaluation harness that does not yet exist.

nodes.label: Prompt Injection Containment via Per-Request Nonce
nodes.rationale: Titles were escaped but bodies were not, so a document containing </source></sources> closed the data block and landed its own text where the model reads it as instruction — reproduced. Fixed with a per-request nonce in the delimiter. Escaping bodies was explicitly rejected because it would corrupt the technical content this corpus is full of, turning <div> into <div> for the model to quote back. Mitigated, not eliminated: a document can still argue with the system prompt, only not impersonate it.

nodes.label: Metadata Double-Encoding Defect (pgvector)
nodes.rationale: The connection registers a jsonb codec whose encoder is json.dumps, and replace_document also called json.dumps, so Postgres stored JSON inside a JSON string and every read produced str where the domain type promises a Mapping. Nothing crashed because nothing checks at runtime, so any future metadata filtering would have failed inexplicably. Found the first time the previously unverified PostgreSQL layer was actually run — exactly the class of bug the untested-storage warning existed to flag.

nodes.label: Prune Data-Loss Guard (unreadable-file exemption)
nodes.rationale: _prune deletes anything indexed but absent from the current sync. A file that failed to parse is absent from the sync yet present at the source, so a corrupt byte — or simply deploying without the `documents` extra installed — would have deleted every PDF from the index, reporting deleted=N as if routine. Loaders now record LoadFailure and the pipeline exempts those ids from pruning, treating them as present-but-unreadable.

nodes.label: Ingestion Data-Loss Defect and replace_document
nodes.rationale: The pipeline wrote the content hash before the chunks in three un-transacted calls; a crash in between left a current hash with zero chunks, so every later sync skipped the document as already-indexed — silently invisible forever while the report counted success. A plain reorder was impossible because chunks reference the document row via a foreign key, so upsert + record_document were replaced with a single transactional replace_document(document, chunks). Notably the protocol got smaller: two methods out, one in.

nodes.label: Chunker Content-Corruption Defect
nodes.rationale: Separators were re-attached as part + separator, appending one to the final fragment that was never there — 287 characters in, 286 out, with a doubled period. In a system whose trust model is 'click the citation and verify', the indexed text was not the source text and the Anthropic path was quoting it back as verbatim evidence. Fixed with a split guaranteeing ''.join(parts) == text.

nodes.label: Parsers Extract and Never Rewrite
nodes.rationale: Chunk text is quoted back as citation evidence, so invented or normalised text would make that evidence a forgery. This is the same trust-model argument that governs the chunker's content-preservation guarantee.

nodes.label: Multi-Format Document Parsing
nodes.rationale: Extension → extraction function: Markdown/text read directly, HTML through the stdlib html.parser (dropping <script>/<style>, preferring the document's own <title>), PDF through pypdf per page retaining page_count, .docx through python-docx including table cells — because policy documents keep the facts people actually ask about inside tables.

nodes.label: Text Extraction Is a Plain Dict, Not a Registry
nodes.rationale: The five component seams use Registry[T] because they are selected by a configuration name and need per-provider options. A parser is selected by file extension and takes no options, so PARSERS: dict[str, Parser] is the whole mechanism. Reaching for the heavier abstraction would have added indirection without removing a line — a direct application of the handbook's 'avoid unnecessary abstractions' rule.

nodes.label: Idempotent Ingestion by Content Hash
nodes.rationale: Content-hash skip, incremental re-index, pruning and per-document failure isolation. Re-running an unchanged corpus makes zero embedding calls, which is asserted by a test and was verified manually (indexed=0 skipped=7 in 0.07s). Known limitation: _prune assumes a single writer — it reads the document-hash map at the start of a sync and deletes anything absent at the end, so a concurrent writer's documents would be deleted.

nodes.label: One Datastore (PostgreSQL holds everything)
nodes.rationale: One PostgreSQL database holds chunk text, embeddings (pgvector), the lexical tsvector index and document metadata. A chunk and its vector cannot drift apart, there is one backup to take, and hybrid retrieval is one round trip instead of a fan-out. A dedicated vector database earns its place only when vector search p95 degrades or the corpus passes a few million chunks.

nodes.label: pgvector Vector Store
nodes.rationale: Largest file in the codebase (379 lines). Applies migrations/001_init.sql through a hand-rolled forward-only runner, substituting the embedding dimension into the DDL at migration time. Verified for the first time against PostgreSQL 18.4 with pgvector 0.8.2: all eleven integration tests pass, covering the migration runner, generated tsvector column, SQL rank fusion, the replace_document transaction, cascade deletion and workspace isolation.

nodes.label: Conditional HNSW Index (2000-dimension limit)
nodes.rationale: CREATE INDEX USING hnsw is capped at 2000 dimensions by pgvector, and the previous default profile specified text-embedding-3-large at 3072 — the first real migration on the old default would have aborted outright. The index is now created only when the dimension is ≤ 2000, with a warning; above it the column is left unindexed and vector search degrades to an exact scan. Correct but O(n), so check this before choosing a wide embedding model.

nodes.label: Vector Width Is Fixed at Migration Time
nodes.rationale: Changing the embedding model changes the vector width, which is fixed in the DDL when the chunks table is created. It requires a new database (or a dropped chunks table) and a full re-index. The store asserts dimensions match at startup and refuses to run otherwise, rather than silently comparing incompatible vectors. This is why every experiment profile names its own database.

nodes.label: workspace_id Partition Key from Day One
nodes.rationale: Explicitly acknowledged as the only speculative design in the codebase, and defended on migration cost: adding a partition key to a populated corpus is a data migration, whereas carrying it now costs one column and one index prefix. Schema-complete and honoured by every query, but single-tenant in practice — only one workspace exists and nothing resolves a workspace from a request.

nodes.label: No LLM Framework (LangChain/LlamaIndex rejected)
nodes.rationale: Evaluated and rejected on evidence, per the stated requirement to judge frameworks pragmatically. The seams this system needs are five protocols totalling about 120 lines; a framework would impose its own document and retriever abstractions on top of ours, add a large transitive dependency tree, and place an uncontrolled layer on the exact code path that most needs tracing and tuning. Provider SDKs are used directly, each as an optional extra.

nodes.label: One Adapter for Eight Services (openai_compatible)
nodes.rationale: OpenAI, Groq, Ollama, vLLM, LM Studio, Hugging Face, OpenRouter and Together all speak /v1/chat/completions, so one adapter is registered under separate provider names with base URL and credential env var pre-filled. Eight adapters would have been eight places to fix the same bug. The single adapter serves 11 registered chat provider names.

nodes.label: Frozen Prompts (module constants, no interpolation)
nodes.rationale: Any dynamic value would break prefix caching for every request and make evaluation results unattributable to a reviewable string. The discipline is kept even though the saving is currently zero.

nodes.label: Prompt Caching — Implemented but Inert
nodes.rationale: cache_system_prompt marks the Anthropic system block cacheable, but ANSWER_SYSTEM_PROMPT is roughly 250 tokens — below the minimum cacheable prefix on current models — so cache_read_input_tokens is zero on every request. Doubly inert now that the default stack is Ollama, which has no such feature. Kept because the discipline is correct and costs nothing.

nodes.label: Reasoning Control Is Configuration, Not Code
nodes.rationale: Qwen3's thinking is disabled with extra_body.reasoning_effort: none through the adapter's existing pass-through for vendor-specific parameters — no new code path, and it works for any reasoning model behind an OpenAI-compatible endpoint. Only the consequences of reasoning needed code (stripping a leaked <think> block before citation parsing, reporting an exhausted budget instead of silently abstaining), because those are correctness concerns rather than tuning.

nodes.label: 4096-Token Context Budget Constraint
nodes.rationale: Ollama loads qwen3:8b with a 4096-token window, which caps the corpus sent to the model at five chunks of ~900 characters. A document needing six passages is answered incompletely rather than incorrectly. chunk_size, top_k and max_tokens are all sized to this window; raising any of them without serving a larger context pushes the answer out of the window.

nodes.label: The Local Model Misreads Figures
nodes.rationale: Observed directly: asked for expense approval thresholds, qwen3:8b rendered the source's '500 to 2,500 EUR' as '50,000 to 2,500 EUR' while citing the correct passage. Retrieval right, citation right, number wrong. The central honest caveat of the local stack: citations tell a user where to check, and on an 8B model they genuinely have to. hosted-anthropic.yaml exists partly as the comparison point for quantifying this gap.

nodes.label: Query Rewriting (implemented, disabled by default)
nodes.rationale: Resolves conversational references into a standalone query using the configured fast model; best-effort, any failure falls back to the original question. Disabled by default because it was never justified by measurement and on the local stack it costs a second Qwen3 call on the critical path. The UI correspondingly sends no history, so follow-up turns are independent questions. Turning both on together is the right move once a golden set can show it helps.

nodes.label: min_score Applied Before Reranking
nodes.rationale: The threshold was being compared against an undefined scale: first-stage scores are on a known scale, but a cross-encoder logit is unbounded and often negative for a relevant passage, so thresholding reranker output would have emptied the result set the moment a reranker was enabled. Now applied to first-stage scores, with a regression test using a negative-scoring reranker.

nodes.label: Evaluation Harness (the highest-leverage missing piece)
nodes.rationale: Designed as a first-class subsystem: 50-100 real questions curated with OSC employees, retrieval metrics (recall@10, MRR) and generation metrics (citation coverage, faithfulness), runnable as `make eval` and gating CI. None of it exists, so every quality claim in the status document is unmeasurable and every retrieval/generation setting in default.yaml is an educated guess. It is the gate for reranking, chunk-size tuning, query rewriting and the local-vs-hosted decision.

nodes.label: OIDC Authentication (not implemented)
nodes.rationale: No identity anywhere; /api/chat and /api/search accept arbitrary unauthenticated input, and a UI at / makes the service look ready to use. Intended design is OIDC against OSC's existing IdP with group membership feeding access control. Smallest interim fix named: refuse to start when environment != development and no auth is configured — ten lines, and the constraint moves from prose into the code path.

nodes.label: Per-Document Access Control (not implemented)
nodes.rationale: Design calls for ACLs resolved at index time and enforced as a SQL predicate at query time, so an unauthorised chunk is never retrieved and never reaches the model. Phase 1 was scoped to company-wide-readable content specifically to avoid needing this yet. Known future limitation: ACLs will be a point-in-time snapshot, so a permission revoked between syncs is not reflected until the next one.

nodes.label: Fully Local Default Stack
nodes.rationale: Ollama qwen3:8b for generation, Ollama nomic-embed-text (768-d) for embeddings, PostgreSQL 18 with pgvector 0.8.2 for storage. No credential required and no corpus text leaves the host. Reference environment verified: PostgreSQL 18.4 / pgvector 0.8.2, Ollama 0.32.5 at a 4096-token context. Note qwen3:8b reports capabilities completion/tools/thinking and cannot embed, which is why a separate embedding model is required.

nodes.label: Speculative Code with No Consumer
nodes.rationale: Flagged as debt: the native Gemini providers are ~330 lines plus a google-genai dependency reaching a service the gemini_openai preset already reaches through a shipped, tested adapter; and FixedSizeChunker is an evaluation baseline for an evaluation harness that does not exist. Both violate the handbook's rule that every abstraction must solve a real engineering problem.

nodes.label: 'local' Provider Name Means Two Different Things
nodes.rationale: In llm_registry `local` is an OpenAI-compatible server on :8000; in embedding_registry it is sentence-transformers. Same token, two unrelated behaviours, coexisting in the same profile file. Proposed fix: rename the LLM one to openai_local.

nodes.label: settings.py Has Zero Tests
nodes.rationale: It carries the only hand-written logic an operator will touch — a custom YAML settings source and four-layer precedence. Nothing verifies that env overrides YAML, that nested OSC_LLM__PROVIDER merges rather than replacing the whole block, or that a missing profile is tolerated. A precedence regression is invisible in tests and surfaces as 'production is running the wrong model'.

nodes.label: Provider Resources Are Never Released
nodes.rationale: Container.shutdown() closes only the vector store. VoyageEmbeddingModel opens an httpx.AsyncClient and defines an aclose() nothing calls; OpenAI and Gemini clients are never closed. Harmless at process exit, a leak in tests and any future in-process reload.

nodes.label: Integration Suite Shares the Application Database
nodes.rationale: Isolation is by workspace_id and is honoured, but a test run against a production DSN would write to production. Also forces OSC_TEST_DIMENSIONS to match the width the chunks table was migrated with (768). Smallest fix: a dedicated test database, and refuse to run when the DSN matches the configured application DSN.

nodes.label: Test Suite (119 tests, 0 skipped)
nodes.rationale: Runs the real pipelines — real container, real retrieval, real answerer — against in-process implementations of the protocols, registered through the ordinary registry, which is the same path a new provider takes. 108 run with no network/DB/credentials; ruff and mypy --strict clean across 45 source files. Three tests are regressions for defects actually reproduced, not speculative. Four material gaps: the end-to-end path is manual, no hosted provider has ever been called, settings.py is untested, and answer quality is unmeasured.

nodes.label: Generated Knowledge Graph and Its Caveats
nodes.rationale: graphify-out/ generated 2026-07-29 from 62 files: 812 nodes, 1973 edges, 36 communities, with wiki/index.md as the agent entry point. Caveats: it predates the parsers/UI/new tests; migrations/001_init.sql is absent because tree_sitter_sql was not installable, so the tables, indexes and the foreign key that forced the replace_document design are invisible; and 135 dangling-endpoint edges, 5 self-loops and 100 collapsed undirected edges mean the edge count understates the raw extraction.

nodes.label: Make the System Verifiable Before Making It Bigger
nodes.rationale: The stated ordering principle for remaining work. The binding constraint has moved from storage (now verified) to measurement, so the evaluation harness is first, then an automated end-to-end smoke test, then auth, then ACLs, then measured retrieval tuning. Deliberately late: the web client, multi-tenancy beyond the partition key, additional providers. Deliberately absent: fine-tuning, agentic tool use, a knowledge-graph layer.
